newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena, Virgin Express to strenghten ties.
newsitem.headline: Sabena, Virgin Express to strenghten ties.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Express regional airline and Belgian flag carrier Sabena are set to sign new codeshare deals for flights from Brussels to Barcelona, Rome and London Gatwick, Sabena said on Thursday.
"It's more than likely (the deals will be signed)," Sabena spokesman Eric Platteau told Reuters. He said the final decision would be taken in the first half of February.
Sabena, owned 49.5 percent by Swissair, has already linked with Brussels-based Virgin Express for flights between Brussels and London Heathrow.
Platteau said the route to Barcelona could be jointly operated from late February, to Rome from March and to Gatwick this summer. The Brussels-Gatwick route would be new for Sabena, he said.

Similar to the first commercial agreement between the two carriers, signed last October, Virgin Express will operate its Boeing 737 planes and crew and offer part of the seats. Sabena will try and sell the rest of the seats.

Platteau said Sabena was satisfied with its cooperation with Virgin Express on its nine flights a day to Heathrow, which enabled the Belgian flag carrier to use three of its own Boeing 737s for longer-distance flights.
He said that traffic between Brussels and Heathrow had remained unchanged from January to September 1996 but had jumped after the deal with Virgin Express.
Traffic between Brussels and Heathrow rose six percent in October, 15 percent in November and 26 percent in December, compared to the month-earlier periods.
He said he could give no financial details but that the Brussels-Heathrow line had been loss-making before the deal with Virgin Express.
"The goal was to make the route profitable, so we should eventually get there," he said.
Sabena will assess its cooperation with Virgin Express in June, he said.
Virgin Express was launched last April after Branson bought 90 percent of Sabena rival EuroBelgian Airlines (EBA).

Recognized by Belgium's labour ministry as a company in difficulty, Sabena had a 1995 group loss before provisions of 530 million Belgian francs ($15.7 million) and a worse-than-expected two billion franc ($59.2 million) net loss in the first half of 1996.
Sabena has repeatedly denied rumours that bankruptcy might be imminent.
In reaction to a report in the Financieel Economische Tijd newspaper on Thursday, Sabena chairman Valere Croes described as "mafia practices" the spreading of such rumours.
According to the rumours, Sabena would be split up after filing for bankruptcy.
Delta Air Lines would take over its transcontinental routes, Swissair the African destinations and Singapore Airlines the link with Tokyo.
Swissair's regional subsidiary Crossair would take over Sabena's regional subsidiary DAT and Virgin Express scoop up the rest of the European network.
($ = 33.8 Belgian francs)
